messages:
incident-bot: [INCIDENT] SEV2 | mem-creep detected on gpu-pool-12 -> node gpu-prod-7. Symptoms: rising OOMs, CUDA errors, autoscaler thrash. Triggered at 6854321890

vivian (oncall): taking this. moving to eng-oncall thread. adding navin and mike. starting triage now.

navin (eng-runtime): on it. preliminary logs show repeated `cudaMalloc failed: out of memory` + allocator fragmentation traces. also seeing slow leak counters on KV cache: `kv_cache.leaked_slots` creeping up. looks like paged-attn allocator fragmentation + KV slot porosity causing gradual memory creep.

mike (oncall): customers are reporting a spike in 5xx/502s and timeouts. suppressing low-priority batch jobs for now. please avoid full daemonset restarts until we have a safe mitigation.

vivian (oncall): navin, can you paste the quick commands you want me to run to gather state?

navin (eng-runtime): run these on the affected node/pod:

```
kubectl -n inference top pod gpu-prod-7
kubectl -n inference logs pod/gpu-prod-7 -c runtime --tail 300 | egrep "cuda|OOM|kv_cache|page_frag"
```

mike (oncall): ran the log commands, pasting the relevant excerpts below.

navin (eng-runtime): logs excerpt: 
"[runtime] cudaMalloc failed: out of memory"
"[allocator] page_frag_stats: total_pages=12345 free_pages=3123 frag_ratio=0.74"
"[kv_cache] evict_rate=0.002 leaked_slots=14"

vivian (oncall): obvious mitigation candidates:
- increase KV cache eviction aggressiveness via env (hotpatch)
- drain node and restart runtime container on gpu-prod-7
- reroute critical traffic off gpu-pool-12 to another pool (eg gpu-pool-9) while we stabilize
Which do we want to try first?

mike (oncall): prefer migration + hotpatch. restarts kill in-flight requests and will cause more 5xxs.

sara (support): heads-up: AcmeAnalytics (cust-1122) opened ticket #4451, seeing job failures and retries tied to this timeframe. Marking P1.

ops-bot: ALERT: us-west-2 routable capacity reduced by 18% after initial autoscale activity on gpu-pool-12.

navin (eng-runtime): applying hotpatch to bump eviction aggressiveness now:
```
kubectl -n inference set env ds/inference-runtime REDWOOD_KV_EVICT_RATE=0.05
```
Watching freed slot counters and OOM frequency.

vivian (oncall): initiating gradual routing policy update to redirect priority traffic to gpu-pool-9. patching routing config now.

mike (oncall): after the evict patch I can already see freed_slots rising (2 -> 9) in ~5m. CUDA OOMs still observed on gpu-prod-7 (likely because some allocations are stuck until container restart).

navin (eng-runtime): agree — need single node restart for the flawed pod. scheduling targeted restart to avoid cascade.

vivian (oncall): performing targeted pod restart: `kubectl delete pod gpu-prod-7 -n inference` — doing now.

ops-bot: NODE UPDATE: pod gpu-prod-7 restarted and entered Ready state. health checks passing.

navin (eng-runtime): post-restart logs show allocator reclaimed pages and kv_cache.leaked_slots down to 1. No CUDA OOMs in the last 2m on that pod. Good sign.

sara (support): AcmeAnalytics acknowledged reduced failures in ticket #4451; they report baseline recovery for retried jobs.

vivian (oncall): summary & action items (assigning now):
- navin: capture heap/profile for the runtime on a repro node and root cause KV slot leak + allocator fragmentation. file follow-up (ENG-###).
- mike: add `kv_leak_rate` and `kv_leaked_slots` metrics to platform dashboard; create alert at threshold X.
- vivian: document hotpatch runbook for `REDWOOD_KV_EVICT_RATE` and safe rollback steps.
- platform: validate routing fallback capacity for gpu-pool migrations (follow-on).

navin (eng-runtime): ack. will add tracing hooks and a regression test that exercises long-sequence attention patterns to catch this class of leak. will open PR with heap dump artifacts.

mike (oncall): closing this incident thread, moving postmortem to ENG board. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATED: severity lowered to P1, incident resolved on gpu-prod-7. Follow-up ticket filed.
